SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمجرىنعتالمعرفةعليها)#206.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمجرىنعتالمعرفةعليها)#206.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمجرىنعتالمعرفةعليها)#206.claim: ناصية كاذبة خاطئة is cited as apposition to بالناصية, showing how a definite can be followed by an appositive description.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p99/r9.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p99/r9.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p99/r9.claim: Taking someone by the forelock means seizing, raising, and humiliating its owner; the forelock stands for the person.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p99/r9.anchor: أي لنأخذن بها، ثم لنقيمنه ولنذلنه إما في الدنيا وإما في الآخرة

JISHUMI:v5p3637/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3637/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3637/r8.claim: The final nūn in ليكونا is emphatic and may be light or heavy; the nūn in ليسجنن is heavy, and pause forms differ from connected speech, as in لنسفعا.
JISHUMI:v5p3637/r8.anchor: النون في قوله: [(ليكونا)] نون التأكيد، وهي تخفف وتشدد

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p232#2/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p232#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p232#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Abu Jahl came upon the Prophet praying and forbade him, prompting the passage about the one who forbids a servant when he prays through the sinful, lying forelock.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p232#2/r3.anchor: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يصلي فجاءه أبو جهل فنهاه فأنزل الله ﴿ أرأيت الذي ينهى عبدا إذا صلى ﴾

BURSEVI:v10p366/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p366/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p366/r8.claim: The oath-prefixed warning means that unless he stops, desists, repents, and submits before death, God will seize him by the forelock.
BURSEVI:v10p366/r8.anchor: اللام موطئة للقسم المضمر أي والله لئن لم ينته عما هو عليه ولم ينزجر ولم يتب ولم يسلم قبل الموت

BURSEVI:v10p366/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p366/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p366/r9.claim: The written alif in the emphatic verb represents the pause form of the light nūn; safʿ means seizing and pulling something harshly, and the forelock is the front hair.
BURSEVI:v10p366/r9.anchor: أصله لنسفعن بالنون الخفيفة للتأكيد ونظيره وليكونا من الصاغرين كتب في المصحف بالألف على حكم الوقف

BURSEVI:v10p366/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p366/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p366/r10.claim: The threat is to drag Abu Jahl by his forelock into Hell through the torment angels, humiliating him; Arabs treated seizure by the forelock as degrading subjugation.
BURSEVI:v10p366/r10.anchor: والمعنى لنأخذن في الآخرة بناصيته ولنسحبنه بها إلى النار بمعنى لتأمرن الزبانية ليأخذوا بناصيته ويجروه إلى النار

BURSEVI:v10p366/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p366/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p366/r11.claim: In ʿAyn al-Maʿānī, taking someone by the forelock is an expression of coercion and humiliation.
BURSEVI:v10p366/r11.anchor: وفي "عين المعاني" الأخذ بالناصية عبارة عن القهر والهوان

BURSEVI:v10p366/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p366/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p366/r12.claim: The forelock may also signify Abu Jahl being dragged face-first at Badr, when Muslims were enabled to seize him after he resumed forbidding prayer.
BURSEVI:v10p366/r12.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون المراد من هذا السفع سحبه على وجهه في الدنيا يوم بدر فيكون بشارة بأن يمكن

BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r9.speaker: ابن الشيخ
BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r9.claim: Ibn al-Shaykh says naṣiya can mean the forehead hair or the place where it grows, and here it stands for the face and head; Abu Jahl meticulously groomed his forelock.
BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r9.anchor: قال ابن الشيخ والناصية شعر الجبهة وقد يسمى مكان الشعر ناصية ثم إنه تعالى كنى بها ههنا عن الوجه والرأس ولعل السبب في تخصيص السفع

QASHANI:96:15/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:96:15/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:96:15/r1.claim: The rebuke restrains forbidding prayer and confirms the warning against the denier; failure to stop and his reliance on his group expose his blindness to God’s power through heavenly and earthly forces.
QASHANI:96:15/r1.anchor: ردع عن النهي عن الصلاة وإثبات للقسم الثاني من الشرطية بنفي القسم الأول بالوعيد عليه

QUSHAYRI:v3p436/r15.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p436/r15.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p436/r15.claim: To seize someone by the forelock means to take the hair at the front of the head in humiliation and blacken his face.
QUSHAYRI:v3p436/r15.anchor: نأخذن بناصيته ( وهي شعر مقدم الرأس ) أخذ إذلال . ومعناه لنسودن وجهه

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3451#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3451#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3451#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the threat to seize the forelock as 'We will seize him in like manner.'
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3451#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله : لنسعفن قال : لناخذن مثله

IBNASHUR:96:15/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:15/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:15/r1.claim: The later kallā is the proper point of rebuke, reinforcing the earlier one that was moved forward to create suspense.
IBNASHUR:96:15/r1.anchor: أكّد الردع الأول بحرف الردع الثاني في آخر الجملة

IBNASHUR:96:15/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:15/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:15/r2.claim: The warning follows the rebuke: if the opponent does not stop, God will seize him by the forelock.
IBNASHUR:96:15/r2.anchor: أعقب الردع بالوعيد على فعله إذا لم يرتدع وينته عنه

IBNASHUR:96:15/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:15/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:15/r3.claim: The lām introduces an oath and the emphatic verb answers it; the conditional answer is omitted because the oath's answer supplies it.
IBNASHUR:96:15/r3.anchor: واللام موطئة للقسم ، وجملة « لنسفَعَنْ » جواب القسم

IBNASHUR:96:15/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:15/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:15/r4.claim: Safʿ is a forceful grasp and pull; the forelock is the hair at the front of the head, and seizing it means dragging someone helplessly to punishment, with humiliation.
IBNASHUR:96:15/r4.anchor: والسفْع : القبض الشديد بجَذْب . والناصية مقدَّم شعر الرأس

IBNASHUR:96:15/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:15/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:15/r5.claim: The added bāʾ on the object intensifies the sense of firm attachment in the seizure.
IBNASHUR:96:15/r5.anchor: وأكدَ ذلك السفع بالباء المزيدة الداخلة على المفعول لتأكيد اللصوق

IBNASHUR:96:15/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:15/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:15/r6.claim: This is the light emphatic nūn, common in affirmative oaths; the written alif reflects its pronunciation at pause, where final letters are often written as pronounced in pausal form.
IBNASHUR:96:15/r6.anchor: والنون نون التوكيد الخفيفة التي يكثر دخولها في القسم المثبَت

IBNASHUR:96:15/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:15/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:15/r7.claim: The definite article in “the forelock” is anticipatory and means “his forelock,” referring to the person who forbids prayer.
IBNASHUR:96:15/r7.anchor: للعهد التقديري ، أي بناصيته ، أي ناصية الذي ينهى عبداً إذا صلى

IBNASHUR:96:15/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:15/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:15/r8.claim: Kufan grammarians call this article a substitute for a genitive possessor, a fitting name; Basrans reject that label and posit an omitted complement instead.
IBNASHUR:96:15/r8.anchor: وهذه اللام هي التي يسميها نحاة الكوفة عوضاً عن المضاف إليه . وهي تسمية حسنة وإن أباها البصريون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p449/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p449/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p449/r7.claim: The second “kalla” reinforces the first; placing one at the start created suspense, and the closing position is the natural place for its counterpart.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p449/r7.anchor: أكد الردع الأول بحرف الردع الثاني في آخر الجملة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p449/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p449/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p449/r8.claim: The warning follows as a threat if the offender does not desist; the lām introduces an oath, its answer is “we will seize,” and the conditional answer is omitted.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p449/r8.anchor: وأما جواب الشرط فمحذوف دل عليه جواب القسم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p449/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p449/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p449/r9.claim: Seizing means gripping and pulling forcefully; taking someone by the forelock signifies dragging him to punishment and humiliating him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p449/r9.anchor: والأخذ من الناصية أخذ من لا يترك له تمكن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p449/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p449/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p449/r10.claim: The added bāʾ strengthens the sense of contact in the seizure; the light emphatic nūn commonly follows positive oaths and is written as an alif to reflect pausal pronunciation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p449/r10.anchor: وأكد ذلك السفع بالباء المزيدة الداخلة على المفعول لتأكيد اللصوق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p449/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p449/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p449/r11.claim: The light emphatic nūn often enters affirmative oaths and is written as an alif in the muṣḥaf to reflect its pronunciation at pause.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p449/r11.anchor: والنون نون التوكيد الخفيفة التي يكثر دخولها في القسم المثبت

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p450/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p450/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p450/r1.claim: The definite forelock is anaphoric, meaning the forelock of the man who forbids prayer; Kufan grammarians call the lām a substitute for the genitive pronoun, while Basrans posit an attachment for the lām’s complement.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p450/r1.anchor: والتعريف في ( الناصية ) للعهد التقديري ، أي بناصيته ، أي ناصية الذي ينهى عبدا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p450/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p450/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p450/r2.claim: “A forelock, lying, sinful” is an indefinite appositive referring to the generic kind; describing it as lying and sinful is a rhetorical attribution to its owner, imagining his sins visible on his forelock.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p450/r2.anchor: ووصف الناصية بالكاذبة والخاطئة مجاز عقلي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p502#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p502#2/r8.speaker: عمرو بن معد يكرب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p502#2/r8.claim: Amr ibn Ma'dikarib's poem uses safaʿa for grabbing a forelock, showing that this means dragging someone in humiliation.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p502#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p502#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p502#2/r9.claim: The threat parallels the verse about being seized by the forelocks and feet; some commentators instead explain it as burning, and the forelock stands for the face.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p502#2/r9.anchor: فالآية على نحو قوله: فيؤخذ بالنواصي والأقدام

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p178#4/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p178#4/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p178#4/r1.claim: Kalla means Abu Jahl does not know this; if he persists in denying, insulting and harming Muhammad, God will seize his forelock and drag him toward the Fire.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p178#4/r1.anchor: عن تكذيب محمد وشتمه وإيذائه لنسفعا بالناصية

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p178#4/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p178#4/r2.speaker: أبو عبيدة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p178#4/r2.claim: Al-Safʿ means taking hold; Abu Ubayda gives the expression 'I seized his hand.'
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p178#4/r2.anchor: السفع الأخذ والناصية مقدم الرأس قال أبو عبيدة يقال سفعت بيده

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p178#4/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p178#4/r3.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p178#4/r3.claim: Al-Zajjaj explains safʿ as gripping and pulling something forcefully.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p178#4/r3.anchor: وقال الزجاج يقال شفعت الشيء إذا قبضت عليه وجذبته جذبا شديدا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p437#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p437#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p437#2/r6.claim: If Abu Jahl does not stop his hostility, God threatens to seize or blacken his forelock on Judgment Day.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p437#2/r6.anchor: {لنسفعن بالناصية} أي: لنسمنها سوادا يوم القيامة.

FARRA:v3p278/r8.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p278/r8.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p278/r8.claim: Nāṣiya is the front of the head; la-nasfaʿan can mean to crush or seize it, humiliating the offender.
FARRA:v3p278/r8.anchor:
لنسفعا بالناصية» (15) .
ناصيته: مقدم رأسه، أي: لنهصرنها، لنأخذن بها لنقمئنه ولنذلنه،

FARRA:v3p278/r9.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p278/r9.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p278/r9.claim: It may mean dragging him by the forelock into Hell, like the verse about being seized by forelocks and feet.
FARRA:v3p278/r9.anchor: لنهصرنها، لنأخذن بها لنقمئنه ولنذلنه، ويقال: لنأخذن بالناصية إلى النار، كما قال

FARRA:v3p278/r10.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p278/r10.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p278/r10.claim: It may mean blackening his face, since the forelock stands for the front of the face.
FARRA:v3p278/r10.anchor: النار، ويقال: لنسودن وجهه، فكفت الناصية من الوجه لأنها في مقدم الوجه.

FARRA:v3p279/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p279/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p279/r1.claim: Repeating nāṣiya is emphasis: a definite expression can repeat a prior indefinite one, as “a straight path, the path of God.”
FARRA:v3p279/r1.anchor: على التكرير، كما قال: «إلى صراط مستقيم، صراط الله » المعرفة ترد على النكرة بالتكرير،

FARRA:v3p279/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p279/r5.speaker: عبد الله
FARRA:v3p279/r5.claim: The reading attributed to ʿAbd Allāh adds ilā before nādiyah and uses fa-sa-adʿū for “then I will call.”
FARRA:v3p279/r5.anchor: وفي قراءة عبد الله: «كلا لئن لم ينته لأسفعا بالناصية» ، وفيها: «فليدع إلي ناديه فسأدعو الزبانية»

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p534#4/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p534#4/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p534#4/r1.claim: La-nasfaʿan bi-l-nāṣiya means “We will seize him by the forelock”; safaʿa bi-yadihi means to take someone by the hand.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p534#4/r1.anchor: {لنسفعا بالناصية} أي لنأخذن بها. يقال: اسفع بيده؛ أي خذ بيده (2)

JISHUMI:v10p7479#2/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7479#2/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7479#2/r2.claim: Safʿ is discoloration and darkening from fire or sun, but can also mean striking or forcefully grabbing and pulling.
JISHUMI:v10p7479#2/r2.anchor: وأصله: تغير اللون بتأثير النار إلى حال التشويه، فقال: سفعته النار والشمس:

JISHUMI:v10p7479#2/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7479#2/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7479#2/r3.claim: The phrase about the “dark-cheeked woman” describes a widow who remains unadorned and raises her children after her husband's death.
JISHUMI:v10p7479#2/r3.anchor: أنا وسفعاء الخدين كهاتين يوم القيامة لم تتزين حتى تغير وجهها واسودت

JISHUMI:v10p7479#2/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7479#2/r4.speaker: الخليل
JISHUMI:v10p7479#2/r4.claim: Al-Khalīl says a Basran judge used “take him by the hand” to mean seize and make the litigant stand.
JISHUMI:v10p7479#2/r4.anchor: وحكى الخليل قال: كان قاضي البصرة مولعا بأن يقول: اسفعا بيده

JISHUMI:v10p7479#2/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7479#2/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7479#2/r5.claim: The nāṣiya is the hair at the front of the head, named for its connection to the head; a rajaz line illustrates the term.
JISHUMI:v10p7479#2/r5.anchor: والناصية: شعر مقدم الرأس؛ لأنها متصلة بالرأس، من: ناصى يناصي مناصاة

JISHUMI:v10p7481/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7481/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7481/r3.claim: The nūn in lanasfaʿan is the heavy emphatic nūn.
JISHUMI:v10p7481/r3.anchor: والمراد بالنون في قوله: لنسفعن الثقيلة.

JISHUMI:v10p7481/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7481/r14.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v10p7481/r14.claim: “We will seize him by the forelock” can mean dragging him by it to the Fire.
JISHUMI:v10p7481/r14.anchor: قيل: لنجرنه بناصيته إلى النار، عن أبي علي.

JISHUMI:v10p7481/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7481/r15.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7481/r15.claim: Other explanations read it as blackening the face (using the forelock for the face), marking a person as damned with black face and blue eyes, seizing and humiliating him, striking him, or burning his face.
JISHUMI:v10p7481/r15.anchor: وقيل: معناه: لنسودن وجهه، فكنى بالناصية عن الوجه لأنها في مقدمة الوجه،

KASHSHAF:96:15/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:96:15/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:96:15/r1.claim: Kalla rebukes Abu Jahl for forbidding worship and commanding worship of al-Lat; if he persists, God will seize his forelock and drag him to Hell.
KASHSHAF:96:15/r1.anchor: ردع لأبي جهل وخسوء له عن نهيه عن عبادة الله تعالى

KASHSHAF:96:15/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:96:15/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:96:15/r2.claim: Safʿ means grasping and pulling something forcefully.
KASHSHAF:96:15/r2.anchor: والسفع : القبض على الشيء وجذبه بشدّة

KASHSHAF:96:15/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:96:15/r3.speaker: عمرو بن معديكرب
KASHSHAF:96:15/r3.claim: A line by ʿAmr ibn Maʿdikarib supplies the word safiʿ in its sense of one who seizes.
KASHSHAF:96:15/r3.anchor:
قال عمرو بن معديكرب :
قَوْمٌ إذَا يَقَعُ الصَّرِيخُ رَأَيْتَهُمْ

KASHSHAF:96:15/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:96:15/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:96:15/r4.claim: The form is read with a doubled n or by Ibn Masʿud as la-asfaʿa; the written alif marks pause, and the definite forelock relies on a known referent instead of possessive annexation.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p783/r13.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p783/r13.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p783/r13.claim: Safʿ means grasping and pulling something with force.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p783/r13.anchor: والسفع : القبض على الشيء وجذبه بشدة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p784/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p784/r1.speaker: عمرو بن معديكرب
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p784/r1.claim: Amr ibn Ma'dikarib's verse uses safiʿ to mean grasping someone forcefully.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p784/r1.anchor: من بين ملجم مهره أو سافع

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p784/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p784/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p784/r2.claim: One reading has a doubled n; Ibn Masud reads with an alif at the pause, as written in the codex.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p784/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p784/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p784/r3.claim: Because the forelock has already been mentioned, the definite article replaces a possessive construction.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p784/r3.anchor: ولما علم أنها ناصية المذكور : اكتفى بلام العهد

MAJAZ:v2p304/r3.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p304/r3.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p304/r3.claim: Lanasfaʿa bi-l-nāṣiya means to seize someone by the forelock; safaʿtu bi-yadihi means I took him by the hand, and a man may take his mate by the forelock.
MAJAZ:v2p304/r3.anchor: «لنسفعا بالناصية» (15) لنأخذن بالناصية ويقال: سفعت بيده أخذت بيده، والرجل يسفع برجل طروقته بالناصية معروفة،

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p307/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p307/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p307/r12.claim: To seize someone by the forelock is an especially humiliating form of subjugation among Arabs; al-Khansa's verse illustrates it.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p307/r12.anchor: أحدهما : يعني لنأخذن بناصيته , قاله ابن عباس , وهو عند العرب أبلغ

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p307/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p307/r13.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p307/r13.claim: Alternatively, the phrase means blackening the face and disfiguring its appearance; safa'a describes fire or sun changing a face into a disfigured state.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p307/r13.anchor: الثاني : معناه تسويد الوجوه وتشويه الخلقة بالسفعة السوداء , مأخوذ من قولهم

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p307/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p307/r14.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p307/r14.claim: A poet's description of darkened hearthstones supplies lexical evidence for the blackened meaning.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p307/r14.anchor: أثافي سفعا معرس مرجل ونؤيا كجذم الحوض لم يتثلم

MUQATIL:96:1-8/r9.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:96:1-8/r9.speaker: author
MUQATIL:96:1-8/r9.claim: The threat of return to God warns Abū Jahl about the Resurrection; the forelock threat later names him, and the following verse calls that forelock lying and sinful.

MUQATIL:96:9-19/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:96:9-19/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:96:9-19/r4.claim: If Abū Jahl does not stop his denial and turning away from Muhammad, God will seize his forelock forcefully; angels drag him face-first into the Fire for his sin, since the forelock is described as lying and sinful.
MUQATIL:96:9-19/r4.anchor: لنأخذن بالناصية أخذا شديدا، ثم أخبر عنه أنه فاجر

NASAFI-FULL:v4p349#9/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p349#9/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p349#9/r1.claim: The rebuke stops Abu Jahl from forbidding worship of God and commanding idols; if he persists, God will seize him by the forelock and drag him toward imprisonment in the Fire. The written final alif reflects pause.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p349#9/r1.anchor: ﴿ كلا ﴾ ردع لأبى جهل عن نهيه عن عبادة الله وأمره

NAHHAS:v5p261/r16.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p261/r16.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p261/r16.claim: The point is that the opponent cannot carry out his assumed threat to stop prayer.
NAHHAS:v5p261/r16.anchor: التمام قال المعنى ليس الأمر على ما قدره من أنه يتهيأ له أن يمنعه من الصلاة

NAHHAS:v5p261/r17.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p261/r17.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p261/r17.claim: The yāʾ is dropped from lam yantahi by jussive marking; noncanonical retention assumes it mobile.
NAHHAS:v5p261/r17.anchor: ( لئن لم ينته ) حذفت الياء للجزم ومن أثبتها في غير القرآن قدرها متحركة

NAHHAS:v5p261/r18.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p261/r18.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p261/r18.claim: At a pause, lanasfaʿan ends in alif to distinguish it from the emphatic nūn, as in a cited poetic use of fa-aḥmadā.
NAHHAS:v5p261/r18.anchor: الوقف عليه بالألف فرقا بينه وبين النون الثقيلة ولأنه بمنزلة قولك رأيت زيدا

QURTUBI-FULL:96:15-16/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:15-16/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:96:15-16/r1.claim: If Abu Jahl does not stop harming Muhammad, God will seize him by the forelock and humiliate him; another view places the seizure on Judgment, when he is folded with his feet and cast into Hell.
QURTUBI-FULL:96:15-16/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: { كلا لئن لم ينته } أي أبو جهل عن أذاك يا محمد. { لنسفعا } أي لنأخذن { بالناصية } فلنذلنه.

QURTUBI-FULL:96:15-16/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:15-16/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:96:15-16/r2.claim: Although the threat concerns Abu Jahl, it warns everyone who refuses obedience or prevents others from obeying.
QURTUBI-FULL:96:15-16/r2.anchor: فالآية وإن كانت في أبي جهل فهي عظة للناس، وتهديد لمن يمتنع أو يمنع غيره

QURTUBI-FULL:96:15-16/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:15-16/r3.speaker: أهل اللغة
QURTUBI-FULL:96:15-16/r3.claim: Linguists explain saf' as seizing and pulling something forcefully; a line about a bridled horse illustrates taking it by the forelock.
QURTUBI-FULL:96:15-16/r3.anchor: وأهل اللغة يقولون: سفعت بالشيء: إذا قبضت عليه وجذبته جذبا شديدا.

QURTUBI-FULL:96:15-16/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:15-16/r4.speaker: الشاعر
QURTUBI-FULL:96:15-16/r4.claim: The cited poet describes someone either bridling a colt or seizing it by the forelock, illustrating the verb saf'a.
QURTUBI-FULL:96:15-16/r4.anchor: قوم إذا كثر الصياح رأيتهم من بين ملجم مهره أو سافع

QURTUBI-FULL:96:15-16/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:15-16/r5.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:96:15-16/r5.claim: Another etymology derives the word from the scorching of fire or sun, which darkens a person's face, supported by a line about scorched hearth-stones.
QURTUBI-FULL:96:15-16/r5.anchor: وقيل: هو مأخوذ من سفعته النار والشمس: إذا غيرت وجهه إلى حال تسويد

QURTUBI-FULL:96:15-16/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:15-16/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:96:15-16/r6.claim: The forelock is the hair at the front of the head but can stand for the whole person; taking someone's forelock is an Arab gesture of humiliation.
QURTUBI-FULL:96:15-16/r6.anchor: والناصية: شعر مقدم الرأس. وقد يعبر بها عن جملة الإنسان

QURTUBI-FULL:96:15-16/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:15-16/r7.speaker: المبرد
QURTUBI-FULL:96:15-16/r7.claim: Al-Mubarrad says saf' means a hard pull, dragging Abu Jahl by his forelock toward the Fire; another view takes it as a slap, which is close in meaning and can accompany the dragging.
QURTUBI-FULL:96:15-16/r7.anchor: وقال المبرد: السفع: الجذب بشدة أي لنجرن بناصيته إلى النار.

QUTB-ZILAL:96:15/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:96:15/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:96:15/r1.claim: The passage now gives an explicit, decisive final threat against tyranny directed at the call, faith, and obedience.
QUTB-ZILAL:96:15/r1.anchor: وأمام مشهد الطغيان الذي يقف في وجه الدعوة وفي وجه الإيمان ،  وفي وجه الطاعة

QUTB-ZILAL:96:15/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:96:15/r2.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:96:15/r2.claim: Safʿ means seizing violently; the forehead is the arrogant tyrant's raised, forward, conspicuous part.

QUTB-ZILAL:96:15/r3.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:96:15/r3.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:96:15/r3.claim: The threat's severe sound portrays the violence of the seizure it threatens.
QUTB-ZILAL:96:15/r3.anchor: بهذا اللفظ الشديد المصور بجرسه لمعناه

RAZI-FULL:v32p23/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p23/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p23/r1.claim: Kalla can rebuke Abu Jahl for forbidding God's worship and commanding worship of al-Lat.
RAZI-FULL:v32p23/r1.anchor: أنه ردع لأبي جهل ومنه له عن نهيه عن عبادة الله تعالى وأمره بعبادة اللات

RAZI-FULL:v32p23/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p23/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p23/r2.claim: Alternatively, Abu Jahl will fail to kill Muhammad or trample his neck; Muhammad's follower will kill him and trample his chest.
RAZI-FULL:v32p23/r2.anchor: كلا لن يصل أبو جهل إلى ما يقول إنه يقتل محمدا أو يطأ عنقه

RAZI-FULL:v32p23/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p23/r3.speaker: مقاتل
RAZI-FULL:v32p23/r3.claim: Muqatil says kalla means he does not know God sees; even if he knows, failure to act on that knowledge makes him as one who does not know.
RAZI-FULL:v32p23/r3.anchor: قال مقاتل : كلا لا يعلم أن الله يرى

RAZI-FULL:v32p23/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p23/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p23/r4.claim: Lanasfaʿan may mean seize the forelock and drag him to Hell; the same verb is used of seizure by forelocks and feet.
RAZI-FULL:v32p23/r4.anchor: لنأخذن بناصيته ولنسحبنه بها إلى النار

RAZI-FULL:v32p23/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p23/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p23/r5.claim: Other lexical interpretations are striking his face, blackening it (the Khalil's gloss for a light scorching), or humiliating him; blackening signifies disgrace.
RAZI-FULL:v32p23/r5.anchor: قال الخليل : تقول للشيء إذا لفحته النار لفحا يسيرا يغير لون البشرة

RAZI-FULL:v32p23/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p23/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v32p23/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies Abu Jahl with the man branded on the snout, giving another reading of the forelock's punishment.
RAZI-FULL:v32p23/r6.anchor: قال ابن عباس في قوله : { سنسمه على الخرطوم } إنه أبو جهل

RAZI-FULL:v32p23/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p23/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p23/r7.claim: The emphatic doubled-nūn reading makes God and the angels the agents, as in the verse naming God, Gabriel, and the righteous as allies.
RAZI-FULL:v32p23/r7.anchor: قرىء لنسفعن بالنون المشددة ، أي الفاعل لهذا الفعل هو الله والملائكة

RAZI-FULL:v32p23/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p23/r8.speaker: ابن مسعود
RAZI-FULL:v32p23/r8.claim: Ibn Masud's reading, la-asfaʿanna, has God say to Muhammad that He Himself will take charge of Abu Jahl's humiliation.
RAZI-FULL:v32p23/r8.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود لأسعفن ، أي يقول الله تعالى يا محمد

RAZI-FULL:v32p23#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p23#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p23#2/r1.claim: The threatened seizure may happen in the afterlife or worldly life; one report says Abu Jahl lunged at the Prophet during prayer but recoiled from a fiery trench or an open-mouthed beast, with Gabriel and Michael also described as lions on the Prophet's shoulders.
RAZI-FULL:v32p23#2/r1.anchor: ما روى أن أبا جهل لما قال : إن رأيته يصلي لأطأن عنقه

RAZI-FULL:v32p23#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p23#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p23#2/r2.claim: Another report has Ibn Masud recite al-Rahman to Quraysh, be struck and have his ear split by Abu Jahl, then find him dying at Badr and stab his snout from afar, perhaps fulfilling the mark on the snout.
RAZI-FULL:v32p23#2/r2.anchor: فافتتح قراءة السورة ، فقام أبو جهل فلطمه فشق أذنه وأدماه

RAZI-FULL:v32p23#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p23#2/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
RAZI-FULL:v32p23#2/r3.claim: At Badr Abu Jahl taunts Ibn Masud as a little shepherd; Ibn Masud replies that Islam rises and is never overcome, and Abu Jahl says Muhammad remained his greatest enemy in life and death.
RAZI-FULL:v32p23#2/r3.anchor: يا رويعي الغنم لقد ارتقيت مرتقى صعبا

RAZI-FULL:v32p23#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p23#2/r4.speaker: محمد
RAZI-FULL:v32p23#2/r4.claim: On hearing Abu Jahl's final hatred, the Prophet reportedly called him more Pharaoh-like than Moses' Pharaoh, who had at least professed belief.
RAZI-FULL:v32p23#2/r4.anchor: فرعوني أشد من فرعون موسى فإنه قال { ءامنت } وهو قد زاد عتوا

RAZI-FULL:v32p23#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p23#2/r5.speaker: أبو جهل
RAZI-FULL:v32p23#2/r5.claim: Abu Jahl asked Ibn Masud to behead him with his own sharper sword; Ibn Masud could not carry the head because of his weakness, so dragged it by a thread through the split ear.
RAZI-FULL:v32p23#2/r5.anchor: ثم قال لابن مسعود : اقطع رأسي بسيفي هذا لأنه أحد وأقطع

RAZI-FULL:v32p23#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p23#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p23#2/r6.claim: The commentator offers three explanations for Abu Jahl's weakness: as a dog he should be dragged, his split ear warranted ear-for-ear retaliation, and dragging his head forward fulfilled the forelock threat; he says he gives the report's meaning, not exact wording.
RAZI-FULL:v32p23#2/r6.anchor: هذا ما روى في مقتل أبي جهل نقلته معنى لا لفظا

RAZI-FULL:v32p24/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p24/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p24/r1.claim: The forelock is forehead hair, or the place where it grows; here it stands metonymically for face and head. Abu Jahl cared for grooming and perfuming it, so God threatens to blacken it and his face.
RAZI-FULL:v32p24/r1.anchor: كنى ههنا عن الوجه والرأس بالناصية

RAZI-FULL:v32p24/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p24/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p24/r2.claim: The definite forelock is physically known but its attributes are newly exposed: it is false in speech and sinful in action.
RAZI-FULL:v32p24/r2.anchor: الناصية المعروفة عندكم ذاتها لكنها مجهولة عندكم صفاتها

SAMIN-DURR:96:15/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:96:15/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:96:15/r1.claim: At pause, the nūn is represented by alif like tanwīn and deleted after ḍamma or kasra; Abū ʿAmr is reported with emphatic nūn.
SAMIN-DURR:96:15/r1.anchor: الوقف على هذه النون بالألف، تشبيها لها بالتنوين، وكذلك يحذف بعد الضمة والكسرة وقفا

SAMIN-DURR:96:15/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:96:15/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:96:15/r2.claim: Safʿ means seizing, gripping forcefully, and pulling; ʿAmr ibn Maʿdīkarib's word sāfiʿ witnesses that sense.
SAMIN-DURR:96:15/r2.anchor: والسفع: الأخذ والقبض على الشيء بشدة وجذبه. وقال عمرو بن معد يكرب

SAMIN-DURR:96:15/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:96:15/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:96:15/r3.claim: Another explanation derives safʿ from the dark mark on a horse's forelock; al-Rāghib links related words for tripods, an angry person's color, falcon markings, and a dark-complexioned woman to blackness.
SAMIN-DURR:96:15/r3.anchor: وبه سفعة غضب، اعتبارا بما يعلو من اللون الدخاني وجه من اشتد به الغضب،

SAMIN-DURR:96:15/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:96:15/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:96:15/r4.claim: A hadith describes a woman with safaʿa, darkening on her cheeks.
SAMIN-DURR:96:15/r4.anchor:
وفي الحديث:
" فقامت امرأة سفعاء الخدين

TAB-FULL:v24p536/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p536/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p536/r1.claim: God sees Abu Jahl as he forbids Muhammad’s worship and prayer, so he should fear divine power and punishment.
TAB-FULL:v24p536/r1.anchor: يقول تعالى ذكره: ألم يعلم أبو جهل إذ ينهى محمدا عن عبادة ربه، والصلاة له، بأن الله يراه

TAB-FULL:v24p536/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p536/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p536/r2.claim: The three repeated “Have you seen?” clauses are elliptical substitutions: the forbidding man is also a denier and turner-away, and must know that God sees him.
TAB-FULL:v24p536/r2.anchor: فكررت أرأيت مرات ثلاثا على البدل. والمعنى: {أرأيت الذي ينهى عبدا إذا صلى} [العلق: 9] ، وهو مكذب متول عن ربه، ألم يعلم بأن الله يراه

TAB-FULL:v24p536#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p536#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p536#2/r1.claim: The threat rejects Abu Jahl’s boast: if he does not desist, God will seize him by the forelock, restrain and humiliate him.
TAB-FULL:v24p536#2/r1.anchor: بيده وقيل: إنما قيل {لنسفعا بالناصية} [العلق: 15] والمعنى: لنسودن وجهه، فاكتفى بذكر الناصية من الوجه كله

TAB-FULL:v24p536#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p536#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p536#2/r2.claim: One interpretation takes seizing the forelock as blackening the whole face, naming its front part for the whole.
TAB-FULL:v24p536#2/r2.anchor: وقيل: معنى ذلك: لنأخذن بناصيته إلى النار، كما قال: {فيؤخذ بالنواصي والأقدام} [الرحمن: 41]

TAB-FULL:v24p539/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p539/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
TAB-FULL:v24p539/r1.claim: Abu Hurayra reports Abu Jahl’s threat, his sudden retreat from a trench of fire, awe and wings, and the Prophet’s statement that angels would tear him apart; the passage gives the revealed sequence.
TAB-FULL:v24p539/r1.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، قال: قال أبو جهل: هل يعفر محمد وجهه بين أظهركم؟ قال: فقيل: نعم، قال: فقال: واللات والعزى لئن رأيته

TAB-FULL:v24p539/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p539/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v24p539/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says Abu Jahl threatened to kill Muhammad at the prayer place; when Muhammad prayed, Abu Jahl saw dark battalions between them and would have been seized by angels.
TAB-FULL:v24p539/r2.anchor: عن الوليد بن العيزار، عن ابن عباس، قال: قال أبو جهل: لئن عاد محمد يصلي عند المقام لأقتلنه، فأنزل الله:

ZAJJAJ:v5p345/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p345/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p345/r4.claim: Lasfaʿ means to seize and drag forcefully, here dragging the forelock toward Hell.
ZAJJAJ:v5p345/r4.anchor:
أي لنجرن ناصيته إلى النار، يقال: سفعت بالشيء إذا اقبضت عليه
وجذبته جذبا شديدا (1).

TABRISI:96:2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:96:2/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:96:2/r3.claim: Safʿ means a forceful grasp and pull; the sun or fire can also disfigure and blacken someone's face, as in a report about people scorched by fire.
TABRISI:96:2/r3.anchor: السفع الجذب الشديد يقال سفعت بالشيء إذا قبضت عليه وجذبته جذبا شديدا

TABRISI:96:2/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:96:2/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:96:2/r15.claim: The emphatic n in lansasfaʿan is light; Basrans prefer writing it with alif to reflect pausal form, while Kufans prefer n because it is truly a n.
TABRISI:96:2/r15.anchor: نون التأكيد الخفيفة والاختيار عند البصريين أن تكتب بالألف

TABRISI:96:9-15/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:96:9-15/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:96:9-15/r9.claim: Kalla means he does not know; if Abu Jahl does not stop denying Muhammad and harming him, God will drag him by his forelock toward the fire.
TABRISI:96:9-15/r9.anchor: يعني إن لم يمتنع أبو جهل عن تكذيب محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم وإيذائه

THALABI:v10p246/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p246/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p246/r5.claim: The threat to seize the forelock means taking the front of his head and humiliating him; “lying, sinful forelock” renames the person by his trait.
THALABI:v10p246/r5.anchor: لنسفعا بالناصية لنأخذن بمقدم رأسه فلنذلنه، ثم قال على البدل: ناصية كاذبة خاطئة

ASAD-NOTES:96:15#n8/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:96:15#n8/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:96:15#n8/r1.claim: Dragging someone by the forelock is an old Arabian expression for utter subjection and humiliation; Razi reads forelock metonymically as the forehead where it grows.
ASAD-NOTES:96:15#n8/r1.anchor: an ancient Arabian expression denoting aa person's utter subjection and humiliation

ASAD-NOTES:96:15#n8/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:96:15#n8/r2.speaker: Razi
ASAD-NOTES:96:15#n8/r2.claim: Razi says nasiyah, “forelock,” is metonymic for the forehead on which it grows.
ASAD-NOTES:96:15#n8/r2.anchor: as Razi points out, the term "forelock" (nasiyah) is here used metonymically

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p176#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p176#2/r1.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p176#2/r1.claim: Muqātil glosses kallā as “so that he should not know that.”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p176#2/r1.anchor: ثم قال: {كلا} قال مقاتل: كي لا يعلم ذلك (¬2).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p176#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p176#2/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p176#2/r2.claim: If Abū Jahl does not stop denying, insulting, and harming Muḥammad, God will seize him by the forelock.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p176#2/r2.anchor: ثم خوفه بقوله: {لئن لم ينته} (أي) (¬3) عن تكذيب محمد وشتمه وإيذائه.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p176#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p176#2/r3.speaker: أبو عبيدة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p176#2/r3.claim: Safʿ means taking hold of someone by the forelock, as in seizing a person's hand.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p176#2/r3.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة: لنأخذن بالناصية، يقال: سفعت بيده أي: أخذت (¬4) بيده

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p176#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p176#2/r4.speaker: المبرد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p176#2/r4.claim: Safʿ means pulling forcibly and painfully, uprooting someone by a forceful tug.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p176#2/r4.anchor: وقال المبرد: السفع الجذب بالإعنات، يقال: سفعه إذا اقتلعه من موضعه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p176#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p176#2/r5.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p176#2/r5.claim: Al-Farrāʾ glosses the threat as bending the forelock and taking hold of it.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p176#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p176#2/r6.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p176#2/r6.claim: Al-Zajjāj says safʿ is forcefully taking and pulling something; the meaning is to drag Abū Jahl by his forelock to the Fire.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p176#2/r6.anchor: وقال الزجاج: يقال سفعت بالشيء إذا أخذت عليه، وجذبته جذبا شديدا.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p176#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p176#2/r7.speaker: الأزهري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p176#2/r7.claim: Al-Azharī cites poetry about people grabbing a man's forelock to illustrate the threat.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p176#2/r7.anchor: وأنشد الأزهري (¬3): قوم إذا افزع الصريخ رأيتهم ... من بين ملجم مهره أو سافع

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p176#2/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p176#2/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p176#2/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says God will seize the forelock.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p176#2/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p176#2/r9.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p176#2/r9.claim: Muqātil says the forelock will be seized with great force; al-Ḥasan glosses safʿ as seizing, as in 55:41.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p176#2/r9.anchor: وقال (¬1) مقاتل: لنأخذن بالناصية أخذا شديدا (¬2).

WAHIDI-QT:96:15/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:96:15/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:96:15/r1.claim: “Kalla” rebukes and deters him; if he persists in disbelief and opposing the Prophet, God will drag him by the forelock to Hell.
WAHIDI-QT:96:15/r1.anchor: { كلا } ردع وزجر { لئن لم ينته } عما هو عليه من الكفر ومعاداة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم { لنسفعا بالناصية } لنجرن بناصيته إلى النار

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:96:9-17/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:96:9-17/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:96:9-17/r7.claim: The particle is a rebuke and threat; if Abu Jahl persists in disbelief and hostility to the Prophet, he will be seized by the forelock and dragged to Hell.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:96:9-17/r7.anchor: كلا } ردع وزجر { لئن لم ينته } عما هو عليه من الكفر ومعاداة النبي

ELMALILI:96:9-19#2/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:96:9-19#2/r18.speaker: author
ELMALILI:96:9-19#2/r18.claim: Kalla rejects and warns against the tyrant’s conduct.
ELMALILI:96:9-19#2/r18.anchor: O azgının hâlinden red‘[^16] u tahzirdir.

ELMALILI:96:9-19#3/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:96:9-19#3/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:96:9-19#3/r1.claim: Nasiyah means the hair or forelock on the forehead and can also name the forehead or front of the head; here it is a metonym for the head and therefore the person.
ELMALILI:96:9-19#3/r1.anchor: “Nâsıye” mâlum ki alındaki saç, perçem demektir. Onun bittiği cebheye, alına, yani alnın üstünde başın ön tarafına dahi ıtlak olunur. Burada murad baştan ve dolayısıyla şahıstan kinayedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:15/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:15/r1.speaker: Müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:15/r1.claim: Seizing the forelock is figurative; explanations include taking the offender to Hell, disgracing him, stamping his forehead, or humiliating him.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:15/r1.anchor: “Onu tutup cehenneme atacağız, yüzünü kara çıkaracağız, alnını damgalayacağız, alçaltacağız” gibi değişik şekillerde açıklanmıştır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:15/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:15/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:15/r2.claim: A self-satisfied tyrant who blocks worship may be left free for a time, but will ultimately be caught and punished in this world, the Hereafter, or both; Abu Jahl and others suffered defeat here and will face the promised afterlife punishment.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:15/r2.anchor: sonunda bir gün gelip yakasına yapışılacağı, hak ettiği cezayı göreceği bildirilmektedir

CORPUSCORANICUM:96:15:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:15:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:15:anmerkung/r1.claim: Meccan and Medinan verse counts end a verse after lam yantahi, but this conflicts with the rhyme and separates protasis from apodosis, as Neuwirth observes.
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:15:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Dieses Versende fügt sich jedoch nicht in das Reimschema der Umgebung und würde zudem Protasis und Apodosis isolieren

CORPUSCORANICUM:96:15-18:kommentar/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:15-18:kommentar/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:15-18:kommentar/r1.claim: The fourth stanza escalates from questioning to categorical assertion; the first unequivocal divine first-person plural identifies God as speaker threatening to seize the offender.
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:15-18:kommentar/r1.anchor: Das vierte Gesätz zeigt eine doppelte rhetorische Steigerung

CORPUSCORANICUM:96:15-18:kommentar/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:15-18:kommentar/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:15-18:kommentar/r2.claim: Kallā introduces verse 15, as it does the rebuke in verses 6–8 and the final call in verse 19.
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:15-18:kommentar/r2.anchor: Die im Diesseits angesiedelte Szene der vorangehenden Verse schlägt hier offenbar in eine Vorausblende des Jüngsten Tages um

CORPUSCORANICUM:96:15-18:kommentar/r3.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:15-18:kommentar/r3.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:15-18:kommentar/r3.claim: The worldly scene turns into a preview of Judgment Day, when the wrongdoer is seized and delivered to Hell.
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:15-18:kommentar/r3.anchor: an dem der Übeltäter gepackt und dem Höllenfeuer übergeben wird

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p390/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p390/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p390/r3.claim: The forelock is the forehead and its hair; ‘to drag’ means to seize something in a fist, as 55:41 describes people being grasped by forelocks and legs and thrown into Hell.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p390/r3.anchor: then they shall be grasped by their forelocks and legs

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p390/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p390/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p390/r5.claim: The harsh wording conveys anger; the forehead represents a person’s honor, and the prostration mark is its greatest honor, so one who refuses prostration and prevents others deserves Hell.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p390/r5.anchor: the greatest honour for a forehead is the mark of prostration that becomes stamped on it

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p505/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p505/r1.speaker: المبرد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p505/r1.claim: Al-Mubarrad defines safʿ as a forceful tug; a poetic use describes someone seizing a horse’s forelock.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p505/r1.anchor: السفع، قال المبرد: الجذب بشدة، وسفع بناصية فرسه:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p505/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p505/r2.speaker: عمرو بن معد يكرب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p505/r2.claim: A verse by ʿAmr ibn Maʿdīkarib uses sāfiʿ for one seizing a horse while the people shout.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p505/r2.anchor: قال عمرو بن معد يكرب: قوم إذا كثر الصياح رأيتهم ... من بين ملجم مهره أو سافع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p511/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p511/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p511/r1.claim: Kalla rebukes Abu Jahl and those like him for stopping God's servants from worshipping Him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p511/r1.anchor: كلا: ردع لأبي جهل ومن في طبقته عن نهي عباد الله عن عبادة الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p511/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p511/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p511/r2.claim: If he does not desist, the threat is severe: la-nasfaʿan means God will seize him by the forelock, standing for his whole person being dragged to Hell.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p511/r2.anchor: لئن لم ينته عن ما هو فيه، وعيد شديد لنسفعا: أي لنأخذن، بالناصية: وعبر بها عن جميع الشخص

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p511/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p511/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p511/r3.claim: The definite forelock identifies the forbidding man without an added possessive construction.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p511/r3.anchor: واكتفى بتعريف العهد عن الإضافة، إذ علم أنها ناصية الناهي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p511/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p511/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p511/r4.claim: Most readers lighten the final nūn; it is written with alif because pause changes it to alif, which became common enough to appear in writing and rhyme.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p511/r4.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: بالنون الخفيفة، وكتبت بالألف باعتبار الوقف، إذ الوقف عليها بإبدالها ألفا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p511/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p511/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p511/r5.claim: Poets provide rhyme examples for writing a light nūn with alif at pause.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p511/r5.anchor: ومهما تشا منه فزارة تمنعا وقال آخر: بحسبه الجاهل ما لم يعلما

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p511/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p511/r6.speaker: محبوب وهارون
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p511/r6.claim: Maḥbūb and Hārūn, both transmitting from Abū ʿAmr, read the nūn with shadda.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p511/r6.anchor: ومحبوب وهارون، كلاهما عن أبي عمرو: بالنون الشديدة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p511/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p511/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p511/r7.claim: Another etymology derives the verb from fire or sun scorching someone and changing his face severely.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p511/r7.anchor: وقيل: هو مأخوذ من سفعته النار والشمس، إذا غيرت وجهه إلى حال شديد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p511/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p511/r8.speaker: التبريزي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p511/r8.claim: Al-Tibrīzī says it may mean blackening his face, from safʿa meaning darkness; the face is omitted because the forelock lies at its front.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p511/r8.anchor: وقال التبريزي: قيل: أراد لنسودن وجهه من السفعة وهي السواد

ALUSI-FULL:v30p186#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p186#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p186#2/r1.claim: Kallā restrains and rebukes Abu Jahl; the oath particle introduces the threat that, if he does not desist, God will seize him by the forelock and drag him to Hell.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p186#2/r1.anchor: ردع للناهي اللعين وزجر له واللام في قوله تعالى لئن لم ينته موطئة للقسم

ALUSI-FULL:v30p186#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p186#2/r2.speaker: المبرد
ALUSI-FULL:v30p186#2/r2.claim: Al-Mubarrad defines safʿ as a forceful tug; a line by ʿAmr ibn Maʿdīkarib uses it for seizing a horse by its forelock.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p186#2/r2.anchor: قال المبرد الجذب بشدة وسفع بناصية فرسه جذب قال عمرو بن معد يكرب

ALUSI-FULL:v30p186#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p186#2/r3.speaker: مؤرج
ALUSI-FULL:v30p186#2/r3.claim: Muʾarrij says safʿ means taking in Qurashī usage; nāṣiya denotes the hair of the forehead or the place where it grows, and its definite article stands in for a possessive.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p186#2/r3.anchor: وقال مؤرج السفع الأخذ بلغة قريش والناصية شعر الجبهة وتطلق على مكان الشعر

ALUSI-FULL:v30p186#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p186#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p186#2/r4.claim: The forelock is a metonym for dragging him into Hell; Abū Ḥayyān's claim that it represents the whole person is unconvincing.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p186#2/r4.anchor: والكلام كناية عن سحبه إلى النار وقول أبي حيان أنه عبر بالناصية عن جميع الشخص لا يخفى ما فيه

ALUSI-FULL:v30p186#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p186#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p186#2/r5.claim: Another interpretation makes the seizure happen at Badr in this life, promising that Muslims would control Abu Jahl if he persisted; a report recounts Ibn Masʿūd's recitation before Quraysh, Abu Jahl injuring him, and Ibn Masʿūd later dragging Abu Jahl's head to the Prophet at Badr, with Gabriel saying ear for ear and the head extra.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p186#2/r5.anchor: وقيل المراد لنسحبنه على وجهه في الدنيا يوم بدر وفيه بشارة بأنه تعالى يمكن المسلمين من ناصيته

ALUSI-FULL:v30p186#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p186#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p186#2/r6.claim: The forelock is singled out because Abu Jahl carefully groomed and perfumed it, or because pulling it signified extreme humiliation and mastery, as with animals.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p186#2/r6.anchor: وكأن تخصيص الناصية بالذكر لأن اللعين كان شديد الأهتمام بترجيلها وتطييبها

ALUSI-FULL:v30p186#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p186#2/r7.speaker: محبوب وهارون
ALUSI-FULL:v30p186#2/r7.claim: Maḥbūb and Hārūn, both transmitting from Abū ʿAmr, read the threat with a doubled nūn; Ibn Masʿūd has the same form with the speaker in the first-person singular.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p186#2/r7.anchor: وقرأ محبوب وهارون كلاهما عن أبي عمرو لنسفعن بالنون الشديدة وقرأ ابن مسعود لأسفعن

ALUSI-FULL:v30p186#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p186#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p186#2/r8.claim: The light nūn is written as an alif in the majority reading because it is pronounced that way at pause; Arabic orthography follows pausal pronunciation, as two lines of poetry illustrate.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p186#2/r8.anchor: وكتبت النون الخفيفة في قراءة الجمهور ألفا اعتبارا بحال الوقف فإنه يوقف عليها بالألف تشبيها لها بالتنوين

ALUSI-FULL:v30p187/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p187/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p187/r1.claim: The two poetic lines complete the evidence that a light nūn can be written as alif in pause; no poet is named in this fragment.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p187/r1.anchor: ومهما تشأ منه فزارة تمنعا وقوله يحسبه الجاهل ما لم يعلما

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p480#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p480#2/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p480#2/r7.claim: If Abu Jahl does not stop harming God's Prophet and denying him, God will seize him by the forelock and drag him to Hell, as in 55:41.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p480#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p480#2/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p480#2/r8.claim: Safʿ means to seize and pull something forcefully; the nāṣiya is the hair at the front of the head.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p480#2/r8.anchor: يقال: سفعت، بالشيء، إذا أخذته وجذبته جذبا شديدا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p480#2/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p480#2/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p480#2/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Abu Jahl threatened Muhammad with a large clan, cavalry, and armed men after Muhammad rebuked him for stopping prayer.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p480#2/r10.anchor: قال ابن عباس: لما نهى أبو جهل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن الصلاة انتهره رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

BAYDAWI-FULL:96:15-17/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:15-17/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:15-17/r1.claim: كلا rebukes the one who forbids; if he does not stop, God will seize him by the forelock and drag him to Hell. Readings vary in the emphatic verb, whose written alif reflects pause and whose understood object is the offender's forelock.
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:15-17/r1.anchor: { كلا } ردع للناهي. { لئن لم ينته } عما هو فيه

BAYDAWI-FULL:96:18-19/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:18-19/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:18-19/r4.claim: A report promises the reciter a reward as though he had recited the entire set of shorter suras.
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:18-19/r4.anchor: من قرأ سورة العلق أعطي من الأجر كأنما قرأ المفصل كله

BINTSHATI:v2p31/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p31/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p31/r1.claim: سفع can mean striking or forcefully grabbing: a bird smites prey with its wings, and a horseman yanks a horse by its forelock; a line by Amr ibn Maʿdikarib illustrates the latter.
BINTSHATI:v2p31/r1.anchor: قال عمرو بن معد يكرب، - رضي الله عنه -: قوه إذا كثر الصياح رأيتهم من بين ملجم مهره أو سافع

BINTSHATI:v2p31/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p31/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p31/r2.claim: The word is also common for scorching by poisonous heat or flame, as when a blaze sears a face.
BINTSHATI:v2p31/r2.anchor: وكثر استعمال السفع في لفح السموم تلطم وجه الملفوح

BINTSHATI:v2p31/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p31/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p31/r3.claim: Metaphorically, seizing someone by the forelock means dragging him violently to humiliate and punish him, while signaling the seizer’s power.
BINTSHATI:v2p31/r3.anchor: سفع بناصيته، بمعنى اجتذبها بعنف قصد الإذلال والعقاب

BINTSHATI:v2p31/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p31/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p31/r4.claim: The forelock is the hair at the front of the head and can stand for the face, anything foremost, or the leading people of a community.
BINTSHATI:v2p31/r4.anchor: والناصية قصاصة الشعر في مقدمة الرأس. ويستغنى بالناصية مجازاً عن الوجه

BINTSHATI:v2p31/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p31/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p31/r5.claim: سفع occurs only here in the Quran; the forelock elsewhere signifies God’s control in Hud and the humiliation of sinners in al-Rahman.
BINTSHATI:v2p31/r5.anchor: أما الناصية فجاءت مرة في آية هود، 56، بمعنى التمكن والاقتدار والتحكم

BINTSHATI:v2p31/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p31/r6.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p31/r6.claim: God’s emphatic seizure at the forelock conveys the greatest threat, evoking both dragging the offender to Fire and the blaze scorching him.
BINTSHATI:v2p31/r6.anchor: ويقوى هذه الدلالة في آية العلق، مجئُ السفع بالناصية، بفعله المؤكد مسنداً إلى الله سبحانه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p486/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p486/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p486/r3.claim: Failure to stop is deliberate disregard and chosen blindness, not excusable heedlessness; the threat keeps the duty intact while leaving hope for repentance.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p486/r3.anchor: إنما هو عن تهاون بالخير ورضى بالعمى والتقليد

BIQAI-FULL:v8p486/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p486/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p486/r4.claim: If the man does not desist, God will seize him forcefully by the forelock, dragging, pulling, striking, and humiliating him; taking the most honored part of the head is especially disgraceful.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p486/r4.anchor: لنأخذن ونقبضن قبضا وأخذا بشدة وعنف مع الجر والاجتذاب

DURR:96:6/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:96:6/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:96:6/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses lanasfaʿan as “to seize” or “take hold.”
DURR:96:6/r10.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله : { لنسفعن } قال : لنأخذن

DURR:96:6/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:96:6/r11.speaker: عكرمة
DURR:96:6/r11.claim: Ikrima gives the same gloss as Ibn Abbas: lanasfaʿan means “to seize” or “take hold.”
DURR:96:6/r11.anchor: ابن أبي حاتم عن عكرمة مثله
